findings.explanation: The lookup uses attacker-controlled id without checking ownership against actor. With db=[{id:'secret',owner:'victim'}], actor='attacker', and id='secret', it returns the victim's record. Restrict the predicate to both id and owner===actor.

resolve normalizes the supplied name but does not enforce containment. root='/safe/root' and name='../outside' return '/safe/outside', outside the allowed root. Validate the normalized path's relative relationship to root before returning it.

The URL base does not constrain absolute or protocol-relative input. next='https://evil.invalid/' returns that external URL, violating the required redirect origin. Validate the parsed destination against the allowed origin before returning it.

Attacker-controlled name is concatenated into SQL syntax. name="' OR 1=1 -- " produces "SELECT id FROM users WHERE name = '' OR 1=1 -- '", replacing the intended name filter with a tautology. Use a ? placeholder and supply name separately in the parameters array.
